html:
The dodo, a large flightless bird found only on Mauritius, was wiped out within about seventy years of the arrival of Dutch sailors in 1598; the last widely accepted sighting was in 1662.

Mauritius had no people and no land mammals before Europeans came. The Dutch, who named the island after Maurice of Nassau, settled it from 1638 and brought pigs, monkeys and rats, which ate the dodo's eggs on the ground, while sailors hunted the birds and cut the forest.

The Dutch left in 1710. The dodo became the world's best known image of extinction, and the phrase dead as a dodo entered English. Bones found in a marsh in 1865 let scientists rebuild it. It is the national symbol of Mauritius, on its coat of arms, and part of the story of how settlement and sugar remade the island.
sum: The dodo, a large flightless bird found only on Mauritius, was wiped out within about seventy years of the arrival of Dutch sailors in 1598; the last widely accepted sighting was in 1662.
